title: The Last Patrol
logline: An aging veteran refuses to stop patrolling a defunct jump gate scheduled for demolition, hiding the fact that their ancient ship is keeping a dormant minefield from waking up.

roles.description: Flies a falling-apart patrol ship, refusing to leave their post long after the war ended.
Bought the rights to the sector's scrap, tired of losing money to a crazy old pilot.
An inactive jump gate scheduled for demolition.
A heavily modified, obsolete fighter held together by duct tape and stubbornness.
Workers trying to dismantle the gate for its valuable metals.

public_situation: The {role:salvage_crew} wants to dismantle the {role:dead_gate} for its valuable metals, but {role:obsessive_veteran} keeps chasing their crews away, claiming the forgotten conflict isn't over.
private_truth: The veteran's ship is continuously broadcasting a containment code to a forgotten autonomous minefield on the other side of the gate. If the ship leaves or the gate is powered down, the mines will reactivate.

beats.public_change: The salvage company puts a public bounty on the old patrol ship to get it out of their way.

missions.reason: The boss needs an armed freelancer to disable the old fighter because their own ships are unarmored salvage tugs.
missions.private_fact: The veteran will offer all their back-pay if the pilot aborts the attack, warning them that the gate isn't safe to touch.

beats.public_change: The salvage crew begins setting demolition charges on the gate.

missions.reason: The veteran's own sensors are shot, and they need a third-party scan to make the salvage crew listen.
missions.private_fact: The scan proves the veteran is telling the truth, but also shows the veteran's transmitter is failing and won't last another week.

player_choice.prompt: The pilot has proof of the dormant mines. The veteran's ship is failing and won't hold them back much longer.

options.label: Give the data to the salvage boss to halt the demolition
Help the veteran detonate the gate permanently

beats.public_change: The veteran begins arming their ship's reactor to destroy the gate.

missions.reason: The veteran needs someone to hold off the salvage ships while they rig the reactor to overload, since they can't fight and prep the detonation at the same time.
missions.private_fact: The veteran intends to die in the blast, seeing it as their final order.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot destroys the veteran's ship, reports the gate is safe, or abandons the defense.
resolutions.summary: The salvage crew cuts power to the gate, breaking the containment signal. Autonomous mines flood through the gate, wiping out the salvage operation before the navy can respond.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot gives the scan data to the salvage boss.
resolutions.summary: The salvage operation is suspended pending a navy review. The veteran remains on patrol, but their ship's transmitter is still dying.

resolutions.reached_by: The pilot holds off the salvage crew while the veteran destroys the gate.
resolutions.summary: The gate is vaporised, sealing the minefield away forever. The veteran is killed in the blast, and the salvage company demands compensation for the lost scrap.

consequences.public_summary: Some old pilot blew up the dead gate to stop ghost-mines from coming through, and a merc covered their six.

loose_threads.detail: The salvage company already pre-sold the gate's unique alloy plating to an anonymous buyer before the demolition was even approved.
The containment transmitter on the veteran's ship uses navy crypto keys that were updated just three months ago.

radio_hooks: Salvage operations at {role:dead_gate} delayed again by 'rogue patrol'.
Local historian claims forgotten conflict automated defenses may still be active.

voice_direction.obsessive_veteran: Gravelly, exhausted, speaks in old military jargon. Refuses to show weakness.
voice_direction.salvage_boss: Impatient, corporate, treats every problem like a line item on a budget.
